outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: The agent’s phrasing around “institution (Offered by)” vs Coursera’s on-page labeling (“Context: IBM”) is a minor labeling difference; the audit conclusion is appropriately cautious (it says audit isn’t clearly confirmable from the visible view), which is acceptable.

Critical issues: (1) Wrong course page/title: DOM-models show the agent was on https://www.coursera.org/learn/python-for-applied-data-science-ai with title “Python for Data Science, AI & Development,” not the requested “Python for Applied Data Science” at https://www.coursera.org/learn/python-for-applied-data-science. The task explicitly asked to open the specific course; reporting details from a different course is not something most users would accept as completing the task. (2) Fabricated/unsupported syllabus details: The agent listed five specific module titles (e.g., “Python Basics; Python Data Structures; …”), but the DOM evidence only shows a summary count “5 modules” and does not show an expanded syllabus or any module titles. That means part of the reported syllabus detail is unreliable.

What the agent did accomplish: It stayed within constraints (no sign-in/enroll/trial), correctly captured instructor “Joseph Santarcangelo,” partner “IBM” (shown as “Context: IBM”), and the visible count “5 modules” for the course page it actually opened. It also correctly noted that an explicit audit option was not visible in the captured view and treated audit availability as not confirmable.

Overall outcome: Because the agent did not actually open/verify the requested course page and additionally reported invented module titles, the user would not have trustworthy, course-specific information for “Python for Applied Data Science.” This is a task failure despite some correct observations on a related page.
outcome.primary_intent: Open the specified Coursera course page and, without signing in or enrolling, extract key overview details: instructor, offering institution, how many modules/weeks are shown in the syllabus, and whether a free audit option is available (or state if it can’t be confirmed). A reasonable user would be flexible about minor wording/formatting, but not about reporting details for the wrong course page or inventing syllabus contents.
